fixes.explanation: That's it. Peter says "…they consider it strange of you not to plunge with them into the same flood of reckless indiscretion…" (1 Peter 4:4) Picture the whole group heading one direction while you stay put. They look at you like you just walked into a cookie swap and left your tray in the car. Strange, friend, is exactly the word.

Peter doesn't point to Caesar or anyone on a throne. He says they "…will have to give an account to Him who is ready to judge the living and the dead." (1 Peter 4:5) That's a much higher seat than any throne. The One who judges is the One Peter names, friend.

Good guess if you were thinking of a big meeting, but Peter doesn't point there. He says they "…will have to give an account to Him who is ready to judge the living and the dead." (1 Peter 4:5) No committee, no agenda, no vote. Just Him.

There it is. Peter says, "Above all, love one another deeply…" (1 Peter 4:8) Above all means he puts it first. The rest of his list, like prayer, hospitality and serving, comes right after it in the same passage. Love sits at the top, friend.

A calendar is handy, friend, but Peter doesn't mention one. He says, "Show hospitality to one another without complaining." (1 Peter 4:9) Nobody's checking a clock at the door. It's about welcoming people without the grumbling, even when the oven's loud and the dough's everywhere.
